summary: Design equitable skills-based talent systems, review AI matching risks, and strengthen internal mobility. Explore the practical five-day course.
lede: Skills-based talent systems training helps HR leaders connect workforce skills data with fairer talent decisions. For CHROs, HR analytics and DEI leaders, and talent acquisition or mobility teams, it addresses how to define skills, assess role matches, and review hiring, promotion, mobility, and compensation decisions. Participants practise competency taxonomy design, work-history skills inference, AI matching and bias checks, and equitable mobility and compensation analysis through spreadsheet exercises and governance planning.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who shape skills data, talent decisions, and fairness controls across the employee lifecycle. This course is designed for: CHROs setting skills-based workforce priorities and reporting talent-system risks. HR analytics leaders developing skills inventories and talent decision dashboards. DEI managers reviewing fairness in hiring, promotion, and compensation processes. Talent acquisition leads assessing skills-based selection and AI-assisted candidate matching. Internal mobility leads designing transparent role matching and employee opportunity pathways. HR business partners translating competency requirements into workforce and career discussions. People data analysts validating employee skills records and matching criteria. Compensation analysts examining pay structures and equity review findings. Talent management specialists aligning competency taxonomies with succession and development processes. AI governance professionals reviewing automated employment decision workflows and oversight controls.
modules: OECD AI Principles and Bias Testing
prerequisites: Prior experience in HR, talent management, people analytics, DEI, compensation, or AI governance is useful. No coding or programming is required. Bring familiarity with at least one talent process, such as hiring, internal mobility, workforce planning, or compensation review. Advanced topics such as AI matching and algorithmic bias assessment are taught at conceptual and operational review levels. The course does not train you to build or deploy production AI models.
